description:
## Summary

Add a GitHub Actions workflow that runs on pull requests and executes the repo's canonical mergeability check, `mise run verify`, on an Ubuntu runner. This repo currently has **no CI at all** (no `.github/` directory exists). This ticket creates the first workflow. It is deliberately scoped to the code-quality check only — no e2e, no packaging, no release jobs.

## Repo context you need (read this first)

Beadsmith is a Tauri v2 desktop app: React 19 + TypeScript frontend (`src/`, Vite, pnpm) plus a Rust crate (`src-tauri/`). Work is tracked in beadwork (`bw`); run `bw prime` before starting.

**Hard repo convention (from AGENTS.md):** all quality commands — lint, format, typecheck, tests — run *only* through the canonical mise task graph in `mise.toml`. Do NOT invoke package scripts or raw tool commands (`pnpm test`, `cargo test`, `pnpm dlx ultracite …`) for quality gates, in CI or anywhere else. The workflow you write must call `mise run verify` and must not redefine any quality command inline.

What `mise run verify` composes (see `[tasks.verify]` in `mise.toml`):

- `ts:check` — Ultracite (oxlint + oxfmt) lint/format check on frontend sources
- `ts:typecheck` — `tsc --noEmit`
- `ts:test` — Vitest unit tests
- `rust:fmt-check` — `cargo fmt --check`
- `rust:clippy` — `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `rust:test` — `cargo test`

`verify` intentionally excludes the Vite/Tauri application build (decision recorded in `bsm-9n1.3`): it is a code-quality check; builds are covered by the e2e scenario pipelines and packaging.

Toolchain pins live in `mise.toml`: node 24.13.0, rust 1.97.1 with profile `default` (includes rustfmt and clippy), and pnpm resolved from `package.json`'s `packageManager` field via `idiomatic_version_file_enable_tools`. Do not duplicate any of these version numbers in the workflow YAML — the mise config is the single source of truth.

## What to build

Create exactly one new file, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:

```yaml
name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Mergeability check (mise run verify)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: Install Tauri Linux system dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libgtk-3-dev libssl-dev \
            libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev pkg-config

      - uses: jdx/mise-action@v3

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: src-tauri

      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build frontend assets (prerequisite for Rust codegen, not a gate step)
        run: pnpm exec vite build

      - run: mise run verify
```

Treat this YAML as the intended shape, not gospel — if the first CI run shows one of these steps is wrong (see "First-run watch list"), fix it and note the correction in the PR description.

## The "why" behind each decision

- **Ubuntu runner, not macOS.** The project owner develops on macOS and runs all checks locally there, so cross-platform CI coverage adds no signal here. Everything `verify` runs is platform-neutral, and Ubuntu runners are faster and cheaper. (The WebDriver e2e suites genuinely need macOS — they use the embedded-WebDriver provider — which is one reason they're out of scope for this workflow entirely.)
- **`jdx/mise-action` for provisioning.** It reads `mise.toml` directly, so Node, Rust (with rustfmt/clippy via the `default` profile), and pnpm all resolve from the repo's own pins. Adding separate `actions/setup-node` / rustup / pnpm-setup steps would duplicate version numbers that would drift from `mise.toml`.
- **`Swatinem/rust-cache` scoped to `src-tauri`.** Without it, compiling the Tauri dependency tree for clippy and `cargo test` dominates CI time on every run. First run ~8–12 min; warm runs should be ~3–5 min.
- **The apt install step is required, not optional.** Tauri's dependency tree includes gtk/glib/webkit `-sys` crates that shell out to `pkg-config` and fail at `cargo check`/clippy time if the system libraries are missing — no bundling has to happen for this to bite. `libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev` is the correct package for Ubuntu 24.04 (current `ubuntu-latest`).
- **The `pnpm exec vite build` step is a prerequisite, not a quality check.** `src-tauri/src/lib.rs:112` calls `tauri::generate_context!()`, which embeds the frontend assets from `../dist` (per `frontendDist` in `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`) **at compile time**. On a fresh CI checkout `dist/` doesn't exist, so all three Rust steps fail. This step is environment provisioning; it does NOT change what `verify` means, and the build must not be added to the `verify` task itself (that's `bsm-9n1.3`'s call). Use `pnpm exec vite build`, not `pnpm build` — the latter prefixes `tsc`, which duplicates `ts:typecheck`.
- **Concurrency group with cancel-in-progress.** Pushing a follow-up commit to a PR cancels the stale run instead of burning runner minutes.
- **`permissions: contents: read`.** Least privilege; the workflow needs nothing else.
- **No `paths-ignore` / path filtering.** Tempting for docs-only PRs, but this check is intended to become a *required* status check (see Follow-up), and required checks that get skipped by path filtering leave PRs unmergeable. Keep it always-running.
- **Deliberately excluded** (do not add, even as "nice to have"): the WebDriver e2e suites (`pnpm test:e2e:*` — intentionally separate per AGENTS.md, macOS-bound, slow), React Doctor and Ultracite Doctor (advisory tools, not gates), and any build/package/release jobs.

## First-run watch list

These are known unknowns you can only resolve by opening the PR and watching the workflow run:

1. **mise trust** — `jdx/mise-action@v3` is expected to trust the repo's `mise.toml` automatically. If `mise run verify` fails with a trust error, add an explicit `mise trust` step before it.
2. **pnpm provisioning** — confirm mise actually resolves pnpm from the `packageManager` field in a fresh CI environment (this works locally, but CI is a clean slate). If pnpm is missing after mise-action, that's the bug to fix — do not work around it with a standalone pnpm setup action without noting why.
3. **apt package names** — correct for Ubuntu 24.04 as of writing; if `ubuntu-latest` has moved, adjust the webkit package accordingly.
4. **`vite build` → `generate_context!`** — confirm a fresh-checkout `dist/` satisfies the codegen (local checkouts have a stale `dist/` that can mask problems).

## Delivery

Per the repo's branch/PR workflow: you already have this ticket; work in a worktree/branch, open a PR against `main`. The PR dogfoods the new workflow — iterate until the `verify` job is green on the PR itself. Before pushing, run `mise run verify` locally. Committing, closing this issue (`bw close`), and syncing are part of completing the task.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `.github/workflows/ci.yml` exists, matching the shape above (or documented deviations from the watch list)
- [ ] The workflow triggers on PRs to `main` and the `verify` job is green on the implementing PR
- [ ] The workflow contains zero inline quality commands — only `mise run verify` plus provisioning/setup steps
- [ ] No version numbers for node/rust/pnpm appear in the YAML
- [ ] No e2e, doctor, build-as-check, or release jobs

## Follow-up (NOT part of this ticket)

After the workflow is green on main, the repo owner will enable branch protection requiring the `verify` status check for PRs to `main`. If you want, note this in the PR description so it isn't forgotten.
title: Add PR-triggered CI workflow running mise verify
